author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): stop the automated PR lanes manufacturing conflicts and missing merges (#580)
body:
* fix(quests): stop the report lane manufacturing its own merge conflicts

Every quest-perfection run rewrote 25 long-settled report pages, so any report
PR that missed its merge window could never be merged again.

`run_url_for()` resolved a page's run link from the slice's ledger `history`,
falling back to the slice's CURRENT run when no entry matched. History is capped
at 20 entries, so every report older than the cap hit that fallback and was
rewritten to whatever run happened to be newest — on every single daily run.
Two runs' PRs therefore conflicted by construction, over bytes nobody authored.

- build_reports_site.py: pin a page's run_url to the one already published
  before falling back. Settled pages become byte-stable, and the link is now
  correct — it names the run that actually produced the walk, not the latest.
- ledger.py: add `merge`, a structural reconciliation of two divergent ledgers.
  The newer slice record wins WHOLESALE (so `perfect` is never merge-derived —
  M7), walk history unions across both sides, and the M6 circuit breaker may
  only tighten. Covered by selftest.
- refresh_report_branch.sh: merge the base branch into a report branch and
  rebuild the ledger + dashboard + collection from their inputs. Refuses to
  resolve anything outside the generated set.

* fix(ci): make the automated PR lanes self-healing instead of one-shot

PR #563 was green on every check and still never merged, then rotted into a
conflict for five days. Two independent h…

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): unbreak Link Health Guardian's lychee step and drop its 12-min fetch (#586)
body:
The weekly full scan has failed since lychee-action v2 started rejecting a
conflicting `output`: the step passed `--output link-check-results/lychee_results.json`
inside `args` while the action's own `output` input still held its default
(`lychee/out.md`). entrypoint.sh exits 1 on that combination:

    Error: 'output' is set in args as well as in the action configuration.
    Please remove one of them.

Drop the `--output` fragment. The JSON the analysis step consumes is not
produced here anyway — scripts/validation/link-checker.py runs lychee itself
(run_lychee writes ${OUTPUT_DIR}/lychee_results.json unconditionally), so this
step's job is the markdown summary, which its defaults already give us.

Also drop `fetch-depth: 0` from the full-scan checkout. Nothing in that job
reads git history: the only `git diff` in link-checker.py is behind
`--changed-only`, which only the PR job uses. In run 30793139884 the
full-history fetch ran 07:18:11 -> 07:30:27 — 12m16s of a 12m24s job.
The PR job keeps `fetch-depth: 0`; it needs origin/BASE_REF...HEAD.

Co-authored-by: claude[bot] <claude[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Amr
subject: content(quests): forge "Bare Metal to Watchtower" dev-server quest with real run evidence (#615)
body:
* content(quests): forge "Bare Metal to Watchtower" dev-server quest with real run evidence

Adds a Level 1000 main quest that walks a bare Debian 13 box end to end into a
hardened, observable development server: reconnaissance, package foundation,
hostname/user/sudo identity, a default-deny firewall with SSH hardening,
per-user Node/Python/Rust toolchains, a restart-safe Postgres/Redis/Adminer
stack, a shared tmux console mirror, and a self-refreshing health dashboard.

Every screenshot is real evidence, not a mock-up. The whole sequence was
executed against a clean debian:trixie-slim container and the service-stack
chapter against a live Docker daemon; the transcripts were recorded as the
commands ran and rendered to terminal images, mirroring how the repo's own
quest-walkthrough tooling seals its evidence. Where the sandbox could not
reproduce real hardware behaviour, the quest says so in a Sandbox note rather
than faking it.

Four defects surfaced during the runs and became teaching content:
- /etc/hosts must carry the new hostname or every sudo call warns
- unquoted --proto =https triggers zsh equals-expansion and breaks rustup
- a health check calling `ufw status` without `sudo -n` reports a false CRIT
  when the dashboard runs as an unprivileged user
- `set-option -g window-size manual` crashed the tmux server outright

Validation: quest validator 100% (77/77, 0 errors, 0 warnings), make
quest-audit passes with generated data in sync, frontmatter validator clean,
make …

* feat(quests): whole-stack, step-by-step sandbox capture for quest walkthroughs

author: Amr
subject: fix(quest-perfection): diagnose auth vs rate-limit, stop red runs from withholding deploys (#641)
body:
The loop failed 8 consecutive daily runs (Aug 17-24) with a misleading
'rate-exhausted' wipeout error: the shared CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is being
rejected at the auth endpoint, but the engine conflated broken credentials
with a refilling rate limit (both raised AuthError -> exit 2 -> 'expected
rate-limit' soft-skip), so the report job red-failed every day with the wrong
message — and each red scheduled run attaches to main's HEAD, which makes
sync-gh-pages withhold the site deploy.

Redesign, layer by layer:

- engine (runner.py): split ThrottleError (sustained rate-limit; refills on
  its own) out of AuthError (invalid/expired/revoked token or billing hold;
  a human must rotate the secret), widen both classifiers, and add a
  preflight() probe that classifies the credential with one tiny call.
- agentic_validate.py: record truncation_reason (auth|rate-limit|cost) in the
  evidence, exit 4 for zero-scored credential failures vs 2 for rate-limit,
  and expose --preflight (0/2/4/1) for workflow gates; loader is now imported
  lazily so the preflight path needs no pyyaml.
- .github/actions/claude-preflight: composite action running that probe;
  fail-open on unclassifiable states so the probe can never become a new
  single point of failure.
- scripts/quest/loop_health.py: the loop's durable alarm — keeps exactly ONE
  open quest-loop-health issue (created/commented, never duplicated; labeled
  needs-human so the issue autopilot routes it to a person) with exact
  rotation ins…

author: Amr
subject: fix(quest-perfection): keep genuinely-unexpected wipeouts loud, not silently green (#643)
body:
Live-testing #641's redesign (first real run since the token was rotated)
surfaced a bug in its own wipeout guard: every zero-productive cause —
auth, rate-limit, AND a genuine engine anomaly — unconditionally exited 0.
A quest hitting the execute engine's max-turns cap (kind=engine, not auth
or rate-limit) opened the quest-loop-health issue as designed, but then
the run went green anyway, contradicting the PR's own stated contract
("red is reserved for the genuinely unexpected") and quietly recreating a
milder version of the original bug: real non-progress with no visible
signal beyond an issue a human has to happen to notice.

Route by cause instead: auth/rate-limit stay green (expected, self-healing
— the whole reason this guard exists, so a dead token can't withhold the
gh-pages deploy). Anything else now fails the job so it stays visible.
This can't reopen a daily-red trap — the ledger's circuit breaker (M6)
already excludes a slice from selection after max_fix_rounds consecutive
imperfect walks, so the same content anomaly reddens at most a few runs
before the loop stops picking it.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Amr
subject: perf(quest-loop): pin Sonnet-class models per stage, adaptive turn budgets, budget-overrun becomes a scored fail (#644)
body:
* perf(quest-loop): pin Sonnet-class models per stage, adaptive turn budgets, budget-overrun becomes a scored fail

Audit of the whole quest-perfection framework against its goal (a routine
quest run of a specific path that a Claude Code OAuth agent executes and
evaluates). The architecture is sound — measurement and repair lanes with
different cadences, workflow-minted sealed evidence, deterministic gates
wherever a model could self-grade, a committed ledger as the contract, and
the self-diagnosing health-issue alarm. Three defects, all fixed here:

1. MODEL ROUTING WAS UNCONTROLLED AND OVERSIZED. The execute engine passed
   no --model at all (floating on the CLI's account default) and every agent
   step inherited _data/ai.yml's Opus fleet default. On subscription (OAuth)
   auth the real economics are rate-window consumption, and the loop's bulk
   work — up to 5 sandboxed quest walks x <=40 turns daily — is squarely
   Sonnet-class agentic tool use. Every quest-lane stage (preflight probe,
   engine walks, walker/fixer agents) now pins ONE model via the
   QUEST_AI_MODEL repo variable (default claude-sonnet-5), engine-side via
   an env-driven --model default and agent-side via ITJ_AI_MODEL into
   run.sh. The gate's preflight probes the pinned model, so it validates
   the exact (credential, model) pair the engine will use. Override without
   a commit: gh variable set QUEST_AI_MODEL --body <model-id>.

author: Amr
subject: feat(quests): per-character skills for the perfection loop's walk + fix lanes (#668)
body:
One Claude skill per character path (.claude/skills/quest-character-<key>/)
carrying the persona, report voice, walk-lens friction checks, per-level
exercise checkpoints, and fix-lens preservation rules for that path. The
quest-walkthrough and quest-fix skills (and the walker/fixer agents) now
resolve the slice's sheet from walk-plan.json's character.key and read it at
their step 3, so both lanes role-play the class consistently.

Accuracy is mechanical: scripts/quest/character_skills.py regenerates each
sheet's roadmap block from _data/quests/paths.yml + quest_registry.py
(make quest-skills), and --check verifies path<->skill coverage, roadmap
freshness, and per-level exercise headings (make quest-skills-check). The
unified quest audit runs the same check as a new advisory 'skills' layer
(non-gating because the audit's PR triggers don't watch paths.yml).

Every sheet states the two-layer voice rule: levels are shared across paths,
so character dialect colors walkthrough narration only - shared quest prose
stays on the quest-fantasy brand profile, and a sheet never expands an
agent's writable surface or overrides an M-rule.

Design note: docs/quests/CHARACTER_SKILLS.md.

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): stop the agentic quest review cancelling itself, skip the deploy PR (#663)
body:
Two independent causes of the same red/wasted-run signal:

1. The main -> gh-pages deploy PR (opened twice daily by sync-gh-pages.yml)
   makes every pull_request workflow fail at startup; filter it by base branch.
2. `labeled` events for non-`agentic-review` labels start runs that are skipped
   by the job `if:` — but concurrency is evaluated first, so they cancelled the
   real review in flight. Give those no-op runs their own concurrency group.
